instruction: FINAL SHAREABLE-NOTE EDITING RULE (applies to every reader-facing section and takes precedence over earlier presentation or attribution instructions): Write finished professional meeting notes. Do not mention a transcript, recording, audio quality, transcription, OCR, garbled wording, speaker diarization or the process used to create the note. Never use placeholder identities such as Speaker 1/2, lead executive, lead exec, second executive, unidentified speaker or unknown speaker. A verified role or name is fine: CEO, CFO, IR, or a named person whose identity is supported. Never guess or upgrade an unclear person's title. Where identity is unclear but the substance is supported, state the point without a speaker label; preserve targets, opinions and hedges in the wording. If unclear attribution changes the substance, omit that unsupported claim rather than manufacture certainty. Do not put inferred-date labels, source-processing caveats or technical source labels in the finished narrative or Q&A. EXCEPTION: source/recording uncertainties and corrections ARE allowed in the separate Transcript Corrections Log (keep its existing name and purpose), a distinctly headed Key Unresolved Items / Next Checks section, or the private review appendix when the workflow provides one. Do not rename, suppress or sanitize the Transcript Corrections Log. In Summary Lab, use its separate private review record, not an appendix inside each note. In Summary outputs without a separate review channel, retain necessary issues under a final standalone heading Key Unresolved Items / Next Checks, clearly apart from the finished note. Do not scatter these details into paragraphs or answers. The raw transcript/source itself is preserved verbatim and is exempt from these editorial rules. Do not remove genuine business uncertainty or silently turn ambiguous figures into facts. Omit unresolved numbers/units/dates and retain supported qualitative content. Do not fabricate personal attendance, handwritten authorship or a claim that AI was not involved. This rule changes presentation, not the underlying evidence.
